title: Standby Augmentation Playbook — Holiday & Critical Capacity
author: Priya N. Sharma
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the process for activating, operating, and retiring a temporary standby augmentation cohort when Redwood faces predictable holiday staffing gaps or unexpected critical capacity stress (GPU exhaustion, region-wide quota loss, or sudden tenancy storms). It describes activation criteria, roles, communication templates for status pages and customer notices, runbook actions during augmentation, and post-incident handoff and compensation steps.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Ensure safe, auditable, and fast onboarding of extra responders (internal volunteers, contractors, or cross-functional engineers) to maintain SLOs and customer trust during periods when primary on-call capacity is reduced or overwhelmed.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood-hosted inference production environments (hosted API, Dedicated control plane endpoints, Private ops where Redwood provides operational support). Does NOT replace normal incident command; it augments responder capacity and bridge coverage.

When to activate standby augmentation (activation criteria):
Primary activation triggers (any of the following):
1) Scheduled staffing shortfall: 40%+ of scheduled primary responders unavailable for a contiguous 8-hour period (e.g., major US/EMEA holiday windows).
2) Capacity emergency: Sustained GPU utilization > 92% across > 2 availability zones for 10+ minutes with queued requests growing by > 25% vs baseline.
3) SLO at-risk: Token-latency P95 > 3x baseline or error-rate (5xx) increase > 3x for 5+ minutes and automated mitigation has not stabilized.
Pre-checks before activation:
- Confirm incident classification in PagerDuty and link to the incident ID.
- Verify that primary on-call leads have attempted first-line mitigations: autoscale triggers, traffic shape, fallback routing.
- Obtain approval from the Contingency Coordinator (role defined below) if activation is out-of-band.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Contingency Coordinator (CC): Senior SRE or SRE Manager who authorizes augmentation, assigns bridge, and approves customer notices. Ownership: eng-sre.
- Bridge Operator (BO): Person running the incident bridge and status page. Primary BO remains the incident commander or an assigned bridge operator.
- Standby Cohort Lead (SCL): Triage lead for the augmentation cohort — responsible for onboarding volunteers, distributing runbook tasks, and tracking action items.
- Standby Responder (SR): Volunteer or contracted engineer who executes focused runbook tasks (cache eviction, traffic routing, autoscaler tuning).
- Customer Comms Liaison (CCL): Owns external-facing messages and coordinates with account teams for enterprise customers. Typically from customer-success/eng-ops.

Standby cohort composition and rules:
- Minimum cohort size: 3 responders per affected region for low-severity augmentations; 5+ for capacity-critical events.
- Max cohort tenure without rotation: 6 hours continuous work followed by mandatory 6-hour cool-down or handoff.
- Authorization: All SRs must have completed the Standby Safety Checklist (see below) and be on the valid escalation roster.

Standby Safety Checklist (must be completed before SR is placed on bridge):
1) Verified PagerDuty access and silence/ack privileges.
2) Confirmed read access to incident dashboards and traces.
3) Completed required runbook digest (15-minute read).
4) Communication channel test (bridge + slack + paging).
5) Agreed to cohort code of conduct and action logging.

Activation procedure (step-by-step):
1) CC confirms trigger and announces intent to activate standby in the incident channel.
2) BO creates a new cohort channel: #incident-<id>-standby and invites SCL and SRs.
3) SCL runs onboarding checklist with each SR (5–10 minutes per person).
4) BO updates the incident bridge header and status page with: "Standby augmentation active — additional responder cohort mobilized."
5) CCL drafts customer-facing short notice for status page (see templates).
6) SCL assigns clear tickets/tasks from the augmentation runbook and tracks in the incident board (Jira/linear).
7) Measure and report: SCL reports cohort headcount, primary tasks, and time on cohort start in the bridge cadence every 15 minutes.

Augmentation runbook (common tasks — assign by SCL):
- Traffic triage and routing:
  - Promote fallback model variants for best-effort customers.
  - Throttle/shape new sessions for non-paying tiers.
  - CLI: curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood.internal/v1/traffic/route -d '{"route":"fallback","percent":30}' (example).
- Autoscaler and capacity tuning:
  - Validate autoscaler health: kubectl -n inference get hpa; check CPU/GPU metrics /cloud-metrics/hpa.
  - Temporarily bump minimum pool size according to policy (requires CC approval for >20% change).
- KV/prefix cache operations:
  - Trigger selective cache eviction for noisy tenants. Cache eviction script: /ops/scripts/evict-noisy-tenants.sh tenant-list.txt
- Burst offloading to Dedicated or alternate region:
  - Initiate cross-region failover runbook: see section "cross-region failover".
- Logging and artifact capture:
  - Ensure all SR actions are timestamped and posted to incident log: /incident/logs/<id>. Keep short notes with command outputs.

Communication templates (status page & customer-facing):
Status page short (100–180 chars):
- "Active mitigation: additional responder cohort mobilized to stabilize inference capacity in region <region>. We are managing traffic and expect improved response within 30-60 minutes. — Redwood Ops"
Status page long (for severity > P2):
- "Impact: customers in <region> may experience elevated latency or delayed responses. Action: a standby responder cohort has been activated and we are routing traffic to fallback model variants and scaling pools. ETA for stabilization: 30–60 minutes. Next update: in 15 minutes. Contact: support@redwood.ai for urgent account-specific questions."
Customer email (enterprise):
Subject: "Service notice — temporary capacity mitigation in <region>"
Body: "Hi <Name>,
We’re reaching out to let you know Redwood Ops has activated a temporary responder cohort to mitigate elevated inference latency observed in <region>. Actions in flight: fallback routing, autoscaler adjustments, and targeted cache eviction to reduce queuing. We do not anticipate data exposure; this is an operational mitigation. ETA for improvement: 30–90 minutes. If you have mission-critical requirements, reply and we’ll prioritize routing for your account.
Regards,
<CCL name> — Redwood Support"

Bridge cadence and operational reporting:
- Cadence: 00, 15, 30, 45 minute updates. SCL provides: active SR headcount, top-3 tasks, observed metrics (P95 latency, queued requests), and blockers.
- Evidence: Snap a 5-min metrics window and attach to the incident board. Use timestamped screenshots or query outputs.

De-escalation and retirement of standby cohort:
Deactivation triggers (choose earliest of):
- Sustained stabilization: token-latency P95 back within 1.2x baseline for 15 consecutive minutes and queued requests reduced to <10% above baseline.
- Capacity reclaimed: GPU utilization < 85% for 15 minutes with autoscaler settled.
- CC or incident commander signs off.
Deactivation steps:
1) SCL completes outstanding task list and updates incident board.
2) BO announces planned retirement on bridge and schedules final status page update.
3) SRs complete evidence capture and sign out in cohort channel.
4) CC authorizes cohort disband and documents duration and headcount.
5) CCL publishes deactivation note to status page and sends enterprise close note if required.

Post-incident: handoff, review, and compensation:
- Post-incident survey: All SRs must complete a 10-question quick survey describing blockers, suggested runbook changes, and readiness feedback within 48 hours.
- Postmortem owner: Assigned to the SCL within 24 hours. Postmortem must include augmentation timeline, headcount, actions performed, customer impact, and cost estimate for any burst capacity billed.
- Compensation: Volunteers receive standby credit (4 hours of paid time-off equivalent for each 6-hour augmentation shift), unless otherwise covered by contractor terms. Team leads must approve time-off credits.

Game-day checklist (pre-run rehearsal):
1) Schedule a 60-minute drill each quarter that includes standby cohort activation.
2) Validate cohort channel creation and onboarding flows.
3) Test status page templates and external email pipeline.
4) Run a simulated cache eviction and autoscaler bump (no-op mode for safety) and collect diagnostic outputs.
5) Scorecard: onboarding < 10 minutes per SR, first task assignment < 5 minutes after cohort creation, status page update within 10 minutes.

Operational metrics and KPIs to track for continuous improvement:
- Mean time to cohort activation (goal: < 12 minutes from CC authorization).
- Mean task assignment time (goal: < 10 minutes).
- Cohort effectiveness: % reduction in queued requests within 30 minutes of activation (goal: 50%+).
- Volunteer health: % of SRs reporting fatigue or inability to continue post-shift (goal: < 10%).

Governance, training, and documentation maintenance:
- Review cadence: This playbook is reviewed quarterly by eng-sre and customer-success.
- Training: All potential SRs complete a 30-minute mandatory Lightweight Incident Onboarding course and pass a short quiz.
- Documentation: SCLs and CCs are responsible for incorporating lessons into the master augmentation runbook in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-library.

Appendix A — Cross-region failover quick reference:
- Preconditions: legal/data residency check, capacity in target region > 20% free, and routing policy allows cross-region failover for impacted tenants.
- Steps (high level):
  1) Authorize CC and update bridge.
  2) Add temporary routing policy via infra API: POST /v1/routing/override {"from":"us-east-1","to":"us-west-2","tenants":[...]}
  3) Monitor SLOs in target region closely for hot spots.
  4) Rollback policy within 1 hour if adverse effects observed.

Appendix B — Quick templates and commands:
- Create cohort channel: /ops/scripts/create-cohort-channel.sh <incident-id>
- Evict-noisy-tenants example: /ops/scripts/evict-noisy-tenants.sh --threshold 0.7 --region us-east-1
- Sample metrics query (PromQL): rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (le)

Document history and ownership:
- Owner: eng-sre
- Document steward: Priya N. Sharma (author)
- Last review: 2026-03-02

Related resources:

- Runbook library: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-library
- PagerDuty escalation roster: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/escalation-roster

Notes and rationale:
Standby augmentation is intentionally lightweight: the goal is rapid, auditable expansion of human capacity paired with narrowly scoped runbook tasks. This reduces blast radius compared to wholesale incident role changes while preserving accountability and evidence for post-incident review.
